answers.answer:
Rice protein in the HMI library has 47 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel and chromium from 3 sources.

What heavy metals are found in rice protein? The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel and chromium in rice protein, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.

Which origins or products of rice protein measured lowest? In one study, total arsenic across 13 groups of rice protein ranged from 82 µg/kg (Protein beverage product labeled rice or brown rice protein) to 230 µg/kg (Dietary supplement, rice protein powders, sample 334093956); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.

Are there legal limits for heavy metals in rice protein? The EU sets a maximum of 1,000 µg/kg cadmium for food supplements (as placed on the market; this is the supplement row, not a rice-protein row). It sets 150 µg/kg inorganic arsenic for non-parboiled milled rice (a grain row, not rice protein) (rice as defined in the regulation). It sets 150 µg/kg cadmium for rice, quinoa, wheat bran and wheat gluten (a commodity row, not rice protein) (commodity row).

How much of the arsenic in rice protein is inorganic? Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 19 results from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.
